content_html:
Traveling by train is the way more comfortable, safe and popular to get to Machu Picchu. The route crosses spectacular landscapes of the Sacred Valley and follows the Urubamba River until reaching Machu Picchu Town (Aguas Calientes).

Currently, there are two authorized companies that operate tourist trains to Machu Picchu, with different services that adapt to all types of travelers.

Essential information about trains to Machu Picchu

Main route: Cusco / Sacred Valley – Machu Picchu Pueblo
Most used station: Ollantaytambo
⏱ Trip duration: 1 hour 30 minutes approx.
Final destination: Hot Waters

From Aguas Calientes you take a 25–30 minute bus to the entrance of Machu Picchu.

Train companies to Machu Picchu

PeruRail

It is the best-known railway company with the highest frequency of daily departures.

Departure stations:

  • Poroy (Cusco – dry season only)
  • Ollantaytambo (Sacred Valley)

Available services:

  • Expedition: economical and comfortable option
  • Vistadome: panoramic windows and snack on board
  • Vistadome Observatory / 360°: panoramic carriage and open balcony
  • Hiram Bingham: luxury train with gourmet food and live music

Ideal for travelers looking for everything from economy to luxury.

Inca Rail

Modern company with comfortable trains and excellent service.

Departure station:

  • Ollantaytambo (includes transportation from Cusco in some services)

Available services:

  • Voyager: economical and comfortable
  • The 360°: panoramic views and semi-open car
  • First Class: spacious seating and food included
  • The Private: exclusive service for private groups

Perfect for those looking for comfort and good service.

Best time to travel by train to Machu Picchu

April – October (dry season)

Stable weather and clear skies
Best views during the trip
Increased train frequency

Book early, especially between May and September.

rainy season

November – March

Occasional rains
Greener landscapes
Fewer tourists

Trains operate normally, but times may vary.
